When I called and made the appointment I did let the receptionist know the reason, but when I got there the GP kept asking for a knee issue that I had no ideea about. Afterwards I got sent out and told to go to a specialist. In 3 weeks a human can die multiple times from infection. When I asked the GP to put down in writing her refusal to provide a prescription she told me to wait 5 minutes at the reception and she will print it there. After 10 minutes of waiting another woman came to me (clinic manager) and told me that the GP I seen earlier has complained that she is scared now because I have threatened her. Seriously? For asking very calmly to provide a paper where she acknowledges her refusal to provide medical care. From my knowledge that is called medical negligence. At the end the GP did put on my file in writing the fact that I was aggressive towards her when I asked a prescription for an more than evident mouth infection. She didn't even looked at me, what to say about a consultation...all I heard is please wait at the reception for 5 minutes tops and you will get your paper there. Not even that. A severe infection in close proximity to the to a vital organ should be a medical emergency, but after 3 weeks of waiting, risking my life giving the fact that it was an infection in close proximity to the soft side part of the head, meaning it could get to the brain in any given time, they're reaction was to make me feel guilty and ashamed because I politely asked for 15 capsules of Amoxacilin 500mg. My thoughts are that the GP (if it was GP) had no ideea what she was doing. I was a qualified nurse and I worked in E.R. Hospital and I have seen a lot, including incompetent doctors, but this is at least the 4th time I am put in the situation where I know more than a doctor does. I AM NOT RECOMMENDING BELMONT MEDICAL CENTRE HEREFORD. Do not attempt to treat yourself or with advice from the Internet or AI. Visit a GP, Taurus, doctor or nurse at ER. Go to ER ONLY IF IT'S AN REAL EMERGENCY AND  NOT FOR ANY bearable pain. Please call the Emergency line in case of chest pain, lack of air, lack of breathing, but please Do Not Abuse the Emergency lines or ER if it's not a real emergency.
